title: World Leaders Split on Democrats' Midterm Win; Burnham Urges Focus on Cost of Living
dek: UK, Spanish, German, South African and Canadian officials responded to the Democratic takeover of Congress, with differing views on what it means for Ukraine, Iran and trade.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: NPR reported that foreign newspapers framed the result as a 'blue wave' or 'blue tsunami'. Russia's state-run Rossiyskaya Gazeta warned that Trump's wrath would fall on Europe after the Republican defeat.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Trump's acceptance of the results gives the world a chance to focus on the cost of living, and said prices cannot fall until the Middle East conflict and Ukraine war are resolved.
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said on social media that American voters rejected policies that 'only impoverish,' and said the far right is 'unraveling.'
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Trump has largely governed by bypassing Congress and would likely keep using executive orders.
Canada's trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said the result will not change Canada's push to reduce economic dependence on the US, and that trade talks will still be held with the White House.
body:
Foreign governments and newspapers reacted on Wednesday to Democrats' takeover of both chambers of Congress, with commentary ranging from celebration to warnings about how a Democratic Congress will affect Ukraine, Europe and trade.

## Press framing

NPR reported that French newspaper Libération called the result 'une vague bleue,' or blue wave, and Britain's Daily Mail called it a 'historic blue tsunami.' The Times of India ran the headline 'midterm blues for Trump.' The Kyiv Independent said the result could be a potential boost for Ukraine. Russia's state-run Rossiyskaya Gazeta took a different view, saying Trump's wrath would fall on Europe after the Republican defeat. Iran's Tehran Times called the election 'Operation Midterms Hammer,' a reference to US strikes on Iran in June 2025.

## Leaders

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the world could now unite around the cost of living. He said prices cannot come down until the conflict in the Middle East and the war in Ukraine are resolved.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez wrote on social media that American society 'voted against policies that only impoverish.' He said the far-right wave is 'unraveling,' citing recent results in Brazil and the United States. Sanchez also faces snap elections he has called for Nov. 29.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said at an event in Berlin that Trump has 'largely governed by bypassing Congress' and that he expects the president to keep using executive orders.

Canada's minister responsible for US-Canada trade, Dominic LeBlanc, said Canada took note of the results but that its effort to reduce economic dependence on the United States will continue. He said trade negotiations will still be held with the Trump White House, not an incoming Democratic-controlled Congress.

South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the Democratic victory heralded a 'new era in world relations' and could help thaw strained ties between Pretoria and Washington.

## Vance and Trump

NPR reported that Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the defeat and welcomed debate over whether it was worth it. Trump agreed that the war had pushed up fuel prices, but said he would go to war again if he had to.

## What is not yet known

The reporting reviewed for this story does not show any formal government policy change in response to the midterms. Foreign officials' comments describe intentions and expectations, not decisions. Meridian will update this story if governments announce policy changes.
